timeline.title: A Short History of Coming of Age
items: Roman boys swapped their childhood toga for a plain white adult one, and the whole family celebrated.
In Britain, turning 21 traditionally meant being trusted with your own front door key. People still give silver keys today.
For the first time, 18 year olds in the UK could vote. Many countries soon did the same.
The United States lowered its voting age to 18 too, and a whole generation got a say.
today: Not in the history books yet. Give it a few years.

letters.title: Advice for the Road Ahead
items: It takes courage to grow up and become who you really are.
Be yourself; everyone else is already taken.
The future belongs to those who believe in the beauty of their dreams.
Do not go where the path may lead, go instead where there is no path and leave a trail.
Often credited to Ralph Waldo Emerson
letters.hand: Good advice, all of it. Ours is simpler: go and be brilliant, {who}.

facts.title: The Science of Turning {age}
items: The brain keeps building its planning and decision making parts until around the mid twenties.
By now you have ridden the Earth around the Sun {age} times, and every lap is nearly a billion kilometres.
By your 18th birthday, your heart has beaten more than 700 million times.
Teenagers really are wired to fall asleep later. Their body clock can shift by up to two hours.
The music we love as teenagers stays with us more strongly than almost any other.
Nobody in history has ever had your fingerprints, or your laugh.
facts.hand: Science can explain a lot. It cannot explain how {who} got this grown up, this fast.
